newsitem.title: FRANCE: French far-right fears third world lacks workers.
newsitem.headline: French far-right fears third world lacks workers.

text.p: France's far-right National Front unveiled an altruistic explanation on Sunday for its plan to ship home millions of immigrants: their poor nations are short of skilled workers.

"Our policy of reversing migratory flows...is based on a simple idea: If France is hard hit by unemployment, Third World nations suffer from a cruel lack of qualified workers," a party working group said.

The proposal was one of many prepared as part of a proposed Front legislative agenda in anticipation of March 1998 general elections in which the Front hopes to gain a foothold in parliament, where it now has no seats.
The proposed programme was being assembled at a three-day congress in Strasbourg, eastern France, ending on Monday.
"Combined with an ambitious training programme, sending immigrants home would thus be of benefit to both parties," the document concluded.

Other working groups drafted proposals ranging from a ban on French participation in European monetary union to a constitutional amendment to give preference in jobs, education and social benefits for "native-born" French people.
One working group, worried about lagging birth rates and fewer marriages, proposed salaries for mothers without paying jobs -- provided that they are of French nationality.
Another group proposed repealing a criminal law punishing inciting racial, ethnic or religious hatred or discrimination -- and granting amnesty to those previously convicted.

The Front working group said the effect of the current law was to prevent the French people from freely expressing themselves in their own land while leaving foreigners free to carry out such practices as polygamy and female circumcision.
